items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The arrangements were by Ernie Wilkins, and it was like Basie's little nine-piece band, the backgrounds that we played.

ctx.x: I was the only white on the date, and this was -- well, the date was Joe Turner's, and the name of the album, which is a collector's item, is The Boss of the Blues.

I think he had asked for all the musicians that they could reproduce from the old days in Kansas City in that association, and I was there because possibly, Joe Jones or somebody from Kansas City who had played with them, didn't, or couldn't make that date, and it took a lot of hello's and explanations -- nobody remembered that I was that kid in Kansas City, and I didn't get any credit on the album, that I was around at the time, so I fit in on that date, I put that badly. The arrangements were by Ernie Wilkins,…

And I settled back and did that record date. But I have had hundreds and hundreds of musicians who have asked me what it was like because it is one of their favorite records. Now that record was reviewed two or three years later, in the New York Times, I believe it was, by a panel and a group of jazz critics; some of them prestigous -- and they picked 80, I believe I have the article someplace , we can't research it now, but they picked 80 of the foremost jazz records of all time, beginning way back, all down…
